title: Sara Duterte's financial transactions need further investigation, says witness
summary: The financial transactions of Vice President Sara Duterte need a further look based on the data submitted by the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLAC), a witness for the defense panel said on…

blocks.text: The financial transactions of Vice President Sara Duterte need a further look based on the data submitted by the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLAC), a witness for the defense panel said on Thursday as the Senate continues to tackle her alleged unexplained wealth.
Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian said that the AMLAC submitted financial transactions made by Duterte from 2007 to 2025. Of which, Duterte had transactions of P2.7 billion from 2009 to 2013.
"Sa mga ganitong data na sinubmit sa amin, hindi ko inimbento ito, ano ang analysis niyo dito?" he asked lawyer Rainer Dela Fuente of AML Consulting PH.
(With data like this submitted to us—I didn't make this up—what is your analysis of it?)
Dela Fuente said that further investigation into the transactions would lead to other processes such as a freeze order and a bank inquiry.

"Ayan po ay it would merit further investigation, your honor. Ayan po ay magti-trigger ng other compulsory processes like freeze order, bank inquiry, so we can dig into the details. Makita sa statement of accounts the actual deposit slips, withdrawal slips," he said.

(That, Your Honor, would merit further investigation. That would trigger other compulsory processes like a freeze order or bank inquiry so we can dig into the details. We can see in the statement of accounts the actual deposit slips and withdrawal slips.)

"Magkakaroon tayo ng conclusion if we get those documents; we gather those documents. As much as possible, no conclusion is being made. We only make the conclusion after exhausting all the legal remedies," he added.
(We will reach a conclusion if we get those documents, if we gather those documents. As much as possible, no conclusion is being made; we only make a conclusion after exhausting all legal remedies.)
The Senate impeachment court is tackling Article 2 of the Articles of Impeachment, which specifically alleges that the Vice President accumulated unexplained wealth through the following:

items: failure to fully and truthfully disclose all her and her spouse's assets, liabilities, and net worth in her statement of assets, liabilities, and net worth (SALN), including in her SALN for the years 2022, 2023, and 2024; and
failure to divest and instead, willfully continued all her business interests during her tenure as vice president for the years 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025.

blocks.text: Moreover, Dela Fuente noted that a closer look into bank documents would be crucial in the case.
"Doon niyo malalaman sino ang pinuntahan, kanino napunta ang pera, ano ang transaction codes," he said.
(I think the bank records, the source documents. There you will find out where it went, who received the money, and what the transaction codes are.)
"Kasi ang CTRs, STRs, these are just snapshots. Hindi niyo nakikita yung mga in between na nangyayari. So makikita niyo 'yan if you dig deeper, makikita niyo 'yan sa bank inquiry," Dela Fuente added.
(Because CTRs and STRs—these are just snapshots. You don't see what happens in between. So you'll see that if you dig deeper; you'll see that in a bank inquiry.)
When asked by Gatchalian if such discrepancies in financial transactions could lead to an impeachable offense, the witness said that it's up to the Senate impeachment court.
"That your honor is a question of law and I would defer again to the honorable impeachment court if it is or it is not an impeachable offense," said Dela Fuente. —LDF, GMA News
